statement.p: Use the Divergence Theorem to calculate the flux of \mathbf{F} across S, where \mathbf{F}=z\boldsymbol{i}+y\boldsymbol{j}+zx\boldsymbol{k}\ and S is the surface of the tetrahedron enclosed by the coordinate planes and the plane \frac x {2} + \frac y {3} + \frac z {4} = 1

static.solution:
(0,0,0),\ (2,0,0),\ (0,3,0),\ (0,0,4) and is described by E = \lbrace(x,y,z) | 0 \le x \le 2, 0\le y \le 3 (1-\frac x {2}), 0\le z \le 4 (1-\frac x {2} - \frac y {3})\rbrace Here we have {\rm div}\ \mathbf{F} = 0 + 1 + x = x + 1, so
\int\int_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \ d \mathbf{S} = \int\int\int_E(x+1)\ dV = \int_0^{2}\int_0^{3(1-\frac x {2})}\int_0^{4(1-\frac x {2}-\frac y {3})} (x+1)\ dz\ dy\ dx = \int_0^{2}\int_0^{3(1-\frac x {2})} (x+1)\left(4(1-\frac x {2}-\frac y {3})\right)\ dy\ dx = 4\int_0^{2} (x+1)\left[(1-\frac x {2})y - \frac 1 {6}y^2\right]_0^{3(1-\frac x {2})}\ dx = 4\int_0^{2} (x+1)\left((1-\frac x {2})\cdot 3(1-\frac x {2}) - \frac 1 {6} \cdot 9(1-\frac x {2})^2 \right)\ dx = \frac 1 2 \cdot 12 \int_0^{2} (x+1)(1-\frac x {2})^2)\ dx = \frac 1 2 \cdot 12 \int_0^{2} (\frac 1 {4} x^3 + \frac 1 {4} x^2 - \frac 2 {2} x^2 + x - \frac 2 {2} x + 1)\ dx = \frac 1 2 \cdot 12 \left[\frac 1 {16} x^4 + \frac 1 {12} x^3 - \frac 2 {6} x^3 + \frac 1 2 x^2 - \frac 1 {2} x^2 + x\right]_0^{2} = \frac 1 2 \cdot 12 \left(\frac 1 4 4 + \frac 1 3 2 - \frac 2 3 4 + \frac 1 2 4 - 2 + 2\right) = \frac {144} {24}
